# First gate: classical fast-forwarding of reversible dynamics

Candidate capability: given neighbor access to a reversible Markov kernel P and initial state x, sample P^t(x,.) or estimate (P^t f)(x) for arbitrary |f|<=1 with work polynomial in sqrt(t), not t. Explicit full-matrix algorithms and full-vector output are different access models and are not ruled out here.

Mechanism tested: replace t transitions by Chebyshev polynomials of degree O(sqrt(t log(1/epsilon))), then sample their signed endpoint measures.

## Exact obstruction to this mechanism
On the infinite d-regular tree (d>=3), let P=A/d. The coefficient of z^k in T_k(z) is 2^(k-1), for k>=1. At each vertex y at distance k from x, all lower powers vanish and P^k(x,y)=d^(-k). There are d(d-1)^(k-1) such vertices. Hence

sum_y |T_k(P)(x,y)| >= [2(d-1)/d]^(k-1).

This holds equally in a finite d-regular graph whose radius-k ball about x is a tree. Any single signed-particle representation W delta_Y with E[W 1(Y=y)]=T_k(P)(x,y) has E|W| >= the displayed norm and E W^2 >= its square. Spectral l2 contraction therefore does not imply usable l-infinity observable variance. This is not a general algorithmic lower bound.

A positive alternative on any d-regular graph is the universal-cover decomposition: delete immediate reversals in a simple random walk. Conditional on reduced length R_t=r, its endpoint is a nonbacktracking r-step walk. R is the birth-death chain 0->1 and, at positive radius, +1 with (d-1)/d and -1 with 1/d. Thus E R_t >= (d-2)t/d. This positive local representation still uses linear expected path length when d>=3. At d=2 it does recover diffusive compression, which is standard one-dimensional structure.

Separate and weaker locality observation: any positive law supported in the radius-r ball has TV error at least Pr(R_t>r) on the tree. This only covers bounded-radius local-output procedures, not explicit-state access or global jumps.

Primary prior art:
- Apers and Sarlette, Quantum Fast-Forwarding: Markov Chains and Graph Property Testing, arXiv:1804.02321. Quantum amplitude preparation and its normalization cost are not classical endpoint sampling. https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02321
- Alon, Benjamini, Lubetzky, Sodin, Non-backtracking random walks mix faster, arXiv:math/0610550. Nonbacktracking/Chebyshev representation is established. https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610550
- Biswas, Pyne,

# Independent capability investigation, 2026-10-10

## Result

A constructive rarity-uniform approximation algorithm for stationary first hitting times to one joint target state in a product of independent heterogeneous two-state continuous-time Markov chains. It avoids both product-state enumeration and simulation of the potentially exponential waiting horizon. It has a proved multiplicative coupling guarantee, absolute CDF-error corollary, and explicit finite-bit specification. Novelty is unverified; the classical decomposition and nearby algorithms are cited. This does not meet an asserted historical-breakthrough threshold.

Main proof: `02_main_construction.md`.
Finite-bit proof/specification: `03_finite_bit_specification.md`.
Numerical implementations are floating-point checks only, not certified implementations.

## Candidate gates

We considered genuinely different capabilities:
1. Classical fast-forwarding of reversible stochastic dynamics by short Chebyshev paths. A regular-tree signed-mass obstruction kills the proposed generic sampling mechanism; see `01_chebyshev_gate.md`. This is not a general algorithmic lower bound.
2. Unbiased differentiation of stationary long-horizon stochastic simulators via coupled interventions and Poisson correction. Direct prior collisions make the broad proposed capability established: Wang--Rhee 2026, arXiv:2606.11487, Theorem 4; Arya--Schauer--Seyer 2024, arXiv:2406.14451; GradInf PLDI 2026. Stopped instead of extending a specialist theorem.
3. Rarity-uniform first-passage clocks. The final selected capability above survived its first constructive and prior-art gates. An intermediate exact Poissonized-clock construction is retained in code but is not the strongest final result.

## Reproduction

Run from this directory:

    python poisson_clock.py
    python compressed_brown.py
    python verify_compressed_clock.py

Fixed random seeds are in the scripts. NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0 were used. Modest CPU only. Results are preserved in the corresponding JSON files.

## Actual numerical evidence

- Explicit full-state reference, n=4, target probability 9.45e-6: 5,000 compressed samples; average 3,193.9 marks and 2.02 large/compressed strata per sample. Across seven specified CDF points, maximum observed discrepancy was 0.01139. Sampling noise remains; this is not a certified error measurement.
- Explicit same-W coupling

# Targeted primary-source boundary

The independent search did not find a theorem matching the complete max-rate-stratified compressed-Cox algorithm and uniform polynomial-bit complexity. This is not a priority determination.

1. Brown's heterogeneous repair-system model and stationary geometric sum are exact prior.
- Brown report, Stanford August 1974: https://statistics.stanford.edu/technical-reports/first-passage-time-distribution-parallel-exponential-system-repair
- Accessible statement: Fill--Lyzinski, Hitting times and interlacing eigenvalues, Theorem 4.1, p. 19: https://www.ams.jhu.edu/~fill/papers/intertwinings.pdf

2. A scalable non-enumerative product-chain algorithm already exists.
- Horvath--Paolieri--Vicario, Approximation of First Passage Time Distributions of Compositions of Independent Markov Chains, 2025: https://qed.usc.edu/paolieri/papers/2025_epew_first_passage_replicated_components.pdf
- It uses an ODE closure treating components as independent after conditioning on non-hitting. The accessed text provides empirical accuracy, not the uniform certified approximation/bit bound here.

3. Related rare-hitting distribution approximations are established.
- Glynn--Nakayama--Tuffin 2020: https://web.stanford.edu/~glynn/papers/2020/GNakayamaTuffin2020.html
- Regenerative simulation and exponential, corrected-exponential, gamma and bootstrap approximations; no matching rate-stratified succinct product-chain complexity result found.

4. Replacing many increments by a mean is established.
- Kawai--Masuda, On Simulation of Tempered Stable Random Variates, section 4.2: https://pstorage-leicester-213265548798.s3.amazonaws.com/18208382/tssim.pdf
- Lévy jump-size truncation/mean replacement differs from the max-spectral-rate strata, but the generic approximation idea must not be claimed new.

5. Scaled mixed-Poisson approximation and zero-mark deletion are established.
- Grabchak--Saba 2025, On approximations of subordinators in Lp and the simulation of tempered stable distributions: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-025-10586-x
- Algorithms 2--3 thin to nonzero Poisson marks of Lévy jumps. Their quantitative theorem has additional characteristic-function integrability assumptions and does not directly cover the zero atom here.

6. Explicit phase-type fast samplers are established but need the large explicit state representation.
